title: Come and Take It

actions.label: Fire the cannon.
actions.detail: Scrap iron and chain, at a hundred men, across a river.

strong.narrate: It goes off with a noise like a barn falling down. It is not clear it hit anything at all. That is the first shot of the Texas Revolution and it may have hit nothing.
strong.broadcast: {name} fired the cannon. The war has started.

partial.narrate: It fires. Something lands in the water well short of the far bank.

weak.narrate: It fires, and the carriage collapses under it, and a man you know is under the wheel.

actions.label: Call the town’s answer loud enough to carry over water.
actions.detail: Four words, and everybody has to hear them.

strong.narrate: Come and take it. It carries. On the far bank a hundred men hear a town refuse, and their commander — who agrees with them about the Constitution — has to decide what to do about it.
strong.broadcast: {name} called the answer across the water. Come and take it.

partial.narrate: It carries. Somebody else was shouting at the same time and it comes out as noise.

weak.narrate: Your voice goes at the wrong moment and the words are gone in the wind.

actions.label: Cross the water and go at them.
actions.detail: This is the part where somebody starts a war on purpose.

strong.narrate: You are across and formed up before they can decide. Nobody dies. That is not because anybody was careful — it is because the man opposite you chose not to make a fight of it.

partial.narrate: You get across wet and disordered and they are already pulling back.

weak.narrate: The crossing is a shambles. If they had wanted a fight this would have been the end of you.

actions.label: Stay with the flag, whatever happens to it.
actions.detail: It is a bedsheet on a pole and it is the only thing everybody can see.

all.narrate: It stays up. Everything anybody remembers about today will have that flag in it, and you are the reason it was still flying at the end.

actions.label: Stop somebody from firing.
actions.detail: There is a man opposite who has not decided yet. Give him the minute.

strong.narrate: You get a hand onto a musket and hold it down for the ten seconds that matter. Castañeda withdraws. Almost nobody is hurt. You will never be able to prove you did anything at all.
strong.broadcast: {name} stopped somebody firing, and the moment passed.

partial.narrate: You slow it down. Somebody fires anyway, further along the line.

weak.narrate: You are shoved aside by a man who has been waiting all week to do this.

actions.label: Count who was actually hurt.
actions.detail: Do it now, before the story sets.

all.narrate: One, perhaps two, and not badly. That is the Battle of Gonzales. It will be told as a battle for the next two hundred years and it was a skirmish that one side chose not to have.

actions.label: Watch them go.
actions.detail: A hundred men, walking away, in good order.

all.narrate: They are not beaten. They are leaving, because their commander decided a general engagement was not worth it, and because he agreed with you about the Constitution. You have won a war that has not started.

actions.label: Get the gun back off the ground.
actions.detail: Whatever happened to the carriage, it happened in front of everyone.

all.narrate: Four of you and a plank. Nobody who writes about today will mention this part.

clock: about six in the morning, and you cannot see fifty yards
